 J U D G M E N T

The petitioners filed claim petitions under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of .90,00,000/- in MVC.No.1412/2023 and .95,00,000/- in MVC.No.231/2024 for the death of Sri.Shankar.M S/o.V.Mani, in road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief is that on 18.02.2023 at about 10.30 a.m., the deceased was proceeding on Splender Pro Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-HS-4502, along with pillion riders i.e., petitioners in MVC.No.231/2024, on National Highway NH-4 Tumkur Road from Dasarahalli towards SRS Junction and when they reached near Opp Jalahalli Metro Station, Bengaluru City, a Verna C/w. 231/2024 Car bearing Regn.No.KA-53-MF-5946, driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the motor cycle driven by the deceased resulting in the accident.
Due to said accident, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Thereafter,
the deceased was shifted to People Tree Hospital, Bengaluru and then shifted to Victoria Hospital at Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and later he succumbed to the injuries.
Thereafter postmortem was conducted and body was handed over to petitioners to performing funeral and obsequies ceremonies.
The petitioners spent .1,20,000/- towards Transportation of body, Funeral and obsequies ceremony and also for medical expenses.
Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and working as Technician at Rollyan Company, Peenya at Bengaluru and earning .30,000/- per month.

Due to untimely death of C/w.
231/2024 deceased, petitioners' life become dark, miserable and depressed and put to great financial hardship.

sentences.text: The petitioners in both the cases stated that the alleged accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car.

The respondents, being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle,
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
3. Upon service of notice, respondent No.1 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed the written statement.
The respondent No.2 did not appear before the tribunal and hence, he is placed as ex-parte.
4. In the written statement, the respondent No.1 denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.1 also denied age, occupation and income of deceased as well as the place, time and manner of accident.
Further it is contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further contended that the claim petition is filed after lapse of 6 months from the date of accident.

The respondent No.1 admitted the issuance of policy bearing No.3311/00874932/000/00 in favour of the second respondent, in respect of Vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-53-MF-5946 and was valid from 25.01.2023 to 24.01.2024 and the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
Further contended that the insured had been willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving license to drive the same as on the date of accident.
Further the driver also not possessing valid permit and fitness certificate to ply his vehicle on the road.

The amount claimed by the petitioners is highly C/w.
231/2024 exorbitant.
Among other grounds prayed for dismissal of the petition against this respondent.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office framed the following:
ISSUES IN MVC.No.1412/2023 1.

Whether petitioners prove that the husband of petitioner No.1, father of petitioner No.2 and son of petitioner No.3 and 4 namely Shankar.M succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 18.02.2023 at about 10.30 a.m., Opp Jalahalli Metro Station, NH-4, Tumakuru Road, National Highway No.4, Bengaluru,
when he was riding a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-HS- 4502, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Car bearing Regn.No.KA-53- MF-5946 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or Award?

In her chief-examination, she deposed that her son was riding the motor cycle slowly and carefully.

In order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of car, the petitioners produced Ex.P1 first information statement lodged brother of deceased by name Sri.Sundareshan.M, with the police on 18.02.2023.
On the basis of first information lodged by brother of deceased, the police registered FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 338 of IPC.

In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent Vendamani vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131929617/

sentences.text: The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The petitioner also furnished spot mahazar and sketch which is marked as Ex.P.3.
The said document discloses that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said document.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The sketch furnished along with mahazar discloses the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Ex.P.4 is the IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to the vehicle are mentioned.
The said document discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The driver or owner of the offending vehicle not provided satisfactory explanation regarding the manner in which damages are caused to the vehicle.
The said document clearly indicates involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 304(A) of IPC as per Ex.P.10.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part C/w. 231/2024 of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioner pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
12. The respondents placed no satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the C/w. 231/2024 documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The respondents placed nothing before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
On perusal of entire record, it discloses that the driver of insured vehicle has driven the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner that resulted in the accident.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.10, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-53-MF- 5946 by its driver and same resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, issue No.1 in both the cases held in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2 in MVC.No.1412/2023 and 231/2024
: Since the issue No.2 in both cases involve common appraisal of materials on record, they are discussed together in order to avoid repetition of facts and evidence.
In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioners are entitled for compensation.

The Tribunal has to consider several factors like age, avocation, income of deceased,
conveyance charges, funeral and obsequies, towards of loss of love and affection, etc., in order to assess the compensation.

(A) Towards dependency and loss of future earnings:
(i) In the petition, the age of the deceased Sri.Shankar.M is shown as 30 years.
In order to prove age of deceased, the petitioners produced Ex.P.11 & 13 - Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card and Driving License.

In the said documents, the date of C/w.
231/2024 birth of deceased is mentioned as 17.03.1992.
The accident occurred on 18.02.2023.
As per recitals of Ex.P.11 & 13, the age of the petitioner is 31 years as on the date of accident.
The respondent No.1, though denied the age of deceased, not furnished any satisfactory materials to disprove the age of deceased, as appearing in Ex.P.11 & 13.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to disprove or rebut the contention of petitioner related to the age of deceased.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioners is to be considered for ascertaining the age of deceased.
On consideration of materials placed before the court, the age of the petitioner is considered as 31 years as on the date of accident.

As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme court of India in Smt.Sarla Verma case,
the multiplier applicable in present case is '16'.
C / w. 231/2024 (ii) The petitioners contended that deceased Sri.Shankar.M was a Technician at Rollon Hydraulics (P) Ltd, Peenya, Bengaluru and earning a sum of .30,000/- per month.

In order to prove the occupation and income of deceased, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.14 - Appointment Order,
wherein it is mentioned that Sri.Shankar.M was designated as Semi Skilled and work entrusted to him as VMC Machine Helper.
As per the said document, the rate of wages payable to him was .17,000/- per month.
Ex.P.15 - Pay Slips for the month of December 2022 and January 2023.
As per Pay slip for the month of December 2022, his Gross Salary was .18,435/- and Net salary was .16,188/-.
As per Pay Slip for the month of January 2023, his Gross Salary was .19,968/- and Net Salary was .17,247/-.
Ex. P.16 is the Bank Statement.
In order to prove these documents, petitioners have not examined the author of these documents.
In the absence of any documents C/w. 231/2024 to show the occupation and income of deceased, notional income is to be taken into consideration.
The petitioners not examined any witness of the establishment in which the deceased was stated to have been employed.
The petitioners not examined the concerned person of the establishment in order to substantiate the documents furnished by them related to occupation and income of deceased.
On consideration of facts and circumstances of case, the notional income of deceased is considered as .16,000/- per month.

sentences.text: In the case on hand, deceased was aged about 31 years.
Hence, in view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, petitioners are entitled for additional 40% to the established income.
The established income of the deceased is .16,000/- and 40% of .16,000/- is .6,400/-.

So, the total gross income of deceased is .16,000/- + .6,400/- =
.22,400/- per month.

The deceased Sri.Shankar.M is married and died leaving behind wife,
children and parents.
In order to prove the same, the petitioners produced notarized copies of Aadhaar cards, which are marked as Ex.P.11.
The respondents not placed any satisfactory materials to disprove C/w. 231/2024 or dispute the relationship of petitioners with that of the deceased.
On perusal of the materials before the Tribunal, it reveals that petitioners No.1 & 2 are the wife and daughter and petitioner no 3 and 4 are parents of deceased.
Respondents not placed any materials to rebut the said documents.
The documents furnished by petitioners in order to show their relationship with deceased, are not controverted by respondents in any manner.
The respondents not placed any satisfactory materials to disprove or doubt the genuineness of said documents or the entries therein.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Court to show that the petitioners are not dependent on the income of deceased.
The materials on record disclose that the petitioners are dependent on the income of deceased.
As such, petitioner No.1 to 4 are considered as dependents on the income of deceased.

As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in C/w. 231/2024 Smt.Saral Verma case where number of dependent of family members is 4 to 6, 1/4th has to be deducted from the gross income of deceased towards his personal expenses and remaining is to be taken as dependency.

In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above C/w.

O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners Under Section 166 of Motor C/w. 231/2024 Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of .34,55,500/- (Rupees Thirty Four Lakhs Fifty Five Thousand Five Hundred only) with interest at 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay to the petitioner.
Respondent No.1 being the insurer are primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

Out of the total compensation amount, the Petitioner No.1 & 2 in MVC in MVC.No.231/2014, being the wife and daughter of deceased, are entitled for 30% each and Petitioner No.3 and 4 in MVC No.1412/2023, being the parents of deceased, are entitled for 20% each.

In the total amount apportioned to the share of petitioners No.1, 60% of the amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1 and the remaining 40% of the amount shall be deposited in her name in any Nationalized bank or Schedule Bank near to her place for a period of 3 years without encumbrance.
As petitioner No.2 is minor, the entire amount apportioned to her share shall be deposited in her name in any nationalized Bank till she attains the age of majority.
Petitioner No.1, being the next friend and natural guardian of petitioner No.2, is entitled for interest that accrues on F.D periodically.
The entire compensation amount allotted to the share of petitioner No.3 & 4 shall be released in their favour.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse C/w. 231/2024 amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA)
and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

opennyai_summary.facts: The petitioners filed claim petitions under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of .90,00,000/- in MVC.No.1412/2023 and .95,00,000/- in MVC.No.231/2024 for the death of Sri.Shankar.M S/o.V.Mani, in road traffic accident.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether petitioners prove that the husband of petitioner No.1, father of petitioner No.2 and son of petitioner No.3 and 4 namely Shankar.M succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident that took place on 18.02.2023 at about 10.30 a.m., Opp Jalahalli Metro Station, NH-4, Tumakuru Road, National Highway No.4, Bengaluru,
when he was riding a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-HS- 4502, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Car bearing Regn.No.KA-53- MF-5946 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or Award?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioner pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
12. The respondents placed no satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the C/w. 231/2024 documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The respondents placed nothing before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
On perusal of entire record, it discloses that the driver of insured vehicle has driven the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner that resulted in the accident.
Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.10, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-53-MF- 5946 by its driver and same resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.

In the absence of materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioners is to be considered for ascertaining the age of deceased.
On consideration of materials placed before the court, the age of the petitioner is considered as 31 years as on the date of accident.
The petitioners not examined any witness of the establishment in which the deceased was stated to have been employed.
The petitioners not examined the concerned person of the establishment in order to substantiate the documents furnished by them related to occupation and income of deceased.
On consideration of facts and circumstances of case, the notional income of deceased is considered as .16,000/- per month.

On perusal of the materials before the Tribunal, it reveals that petitioners No.1 & 2 are the wife and daughter and petitioner no 3 and 4 are parents of deceased.
Respondents not placed any materials to rebut the said documents.
The documents furnished by petitioners in order to show their relationship with deceased, are not controverted by respondents in any manner.
The respondents not placed any satisfactory materials to disprove or doubt the genuineness of said documents or the entries therein.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Court to show that the petitioners are not dependent on the income of deceased.
The materials on record disclose that the petitioners are dependent on the income of deceased.
So, in view of Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Pranay Sethi's case and the decision rendered on 30th October 2017 between United India Insurance Co. Ltd V/s Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others in Civil Appeal No.2705 of 2020 & in between National insurance company LTD C/w. 231/2024 V/s Pranay Vendamani vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131929617/
8 Sethi and Ors., the petitioners are entitled for additional 10% on conventional heads which is to be enhanced on percentage basis in every three years and the enhancement should be at the rate of 10%
in a span of three years.

17. Issue No.3 in both the cases
: In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners Under Section 166 of Motor C/w. 231/2024 Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of .34,55,500/- (Rupees Thirty Four Lakhs Fifty Five Thousand Five Hundred only) with interest at 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay to the petitioner.
Respondent No.1 being the insurer are primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Out of the total compensation amount, the Petitioner No.1 & 2 in MVC in MVC.No.231/2014, being the wife and daughter of deceased, are entitled for 30% each and Petitioner No.3 and 4 in MVC No.1412/2023, being the parents of deceased, are entitled for 20% each.
C/w. 231/2024
In the total amount apportioned to the share of petitioners No.1, 60% of the amount shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1 and the remaining 40% of the amount shall be deposited in her name in any Nationalized bank or Schedule Bank near to her place for a period of 3 years without encumbrance.
As petitioner No.2 is minor, the entire amount apportioned to her share shall be deposited in her name in any nationalized Bank till she attains the age of majority.
Petitioner No.1, being the next friend and natural guardian of petitioner No.2, is entitled for interest that accrues on F.D periodically.
The entire compensation amount allotted to the share of petitioner No.3 & 4 shall be released in their favour.
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse C/w. 231/2024 amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA)
and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.
The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall Vendamani vs Cholamandalam Ms Gen Ins Co Ltd on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131929617/
10 produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded  amount with interest thereon by  respondent, the petitioner is  entitled to receive amount as  mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature C/w. 231/2024 release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to his account after expiry of three years period of deposit,
without waiting for further order of court.
The Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/- in each case.
Draw awards accordingly.
The original Judgment shall be kept in MVC.No.1412/2023.
